# Heirloom

> Heirloom is a self-custody crypto inheritance and wallet recovery protocol on Solana. You lock SOL and SPL tokens in an on-chain estate, check in on a schedule you choose, and if the check-ins stop, the heir you named (another person, or a backup wallet of your own) claims the estate on-chain. No custodian, no lawyer, and no shared seed phrase.

Key facts:

- Non-custodial: estate accounts are program-derived, so only the Heirloom program can move funds, and there are no admin instructions.
- The deadline: an estate becomes claimable at last check-in + check-in interval + grace period. The owner can take everything back at any time before the heir claims.
- Optional roles: a guardian who can pause the deadline once, and a check-in signer who can check in for the owner.
- Fees: opening an estate, adding SOL or tokens and checking in are free. 10% of yield earned, 0.75% when an heir claims, 0.5% when the owner closes an estate, 0.01 SOL per NFT added.
- Not a legal will: Heirloom is programmable self-custody continuity, a complement to estate planning.
